events.title: Dante Alighieri Dies in Ravenna
events.description: The Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy died in Ravenna, the city where he spent his final years in exile from his native Florence. He was about 56.
events.significance: Dante's epic journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise became a cornerstone of world literature. It helped establish the Tuscan dialect as the foundation of the modern Italian language.

events.title: Britain Adopts the Gregorian Calendar
events.description: Britain and its American colonies switched from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar. Eleven days were skipped, so the day after September 2 was September 14.
events.significance: The change aligned the British world with most of Europe and fixed years of calendar drift. It also gave rise to the enduring legend of people demanding their 'lost' eleven days.

events.title: Napoleon's Grande Armée Enters Moscow
events.description: French forces marched into Moscow during Napoleon's invasion of Russia. The city was largely emptied of its residents, and fires soon broke out across it.
events.significance: Napoleon found no surrender and no supplies. His long, costly retreat in the winter that followed destroyed much of his army and marked a turning point in his fortunes.

events.title: 'The Star-Spangled Banner' Is Written
events.description: After watching the British bombardment of Fort McHenry in Baltimore, lawyer Francis Scott Key saw the American flag still flying at dawn. He was inspired to write the poem that became the U.S. national anthem.
events.significance: Set to music, the poem became a national symbol. Congress made it the official anthem of the United States in 1931.

events.title: President William McKinley Dies
events.description: Eight days after being shot by an assassin at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, President William McKinley died of complications from his wounds.
events.significance: His death elevated Theodore Roosevelt, then 42, to the presidency. Roosevelt's tenure reshaped American politics and expanded the role of the federal government.
